page_title: Bookmark Manager for Mac That Searches by Meaning | Unbury

summary.name: Unbury
summary.one_liner: Open-source Mac bookmark manager that finds saved browser bookmarks by meaning rather than exact title or word matches.
use_cases: Finding a saved page when you remember what it was about but not its title
Searching a large bookmark collection by topic and time range
Checking whether a similar link is already saved before bookmarking it again
Asking natural-language questions over saved links
summary.what_it_does: Unbury imports bookmarks from Brave, Chrome, Arc, Edge and Vivaldi profiles on a Mac, then describes each link with a model and stores a vector for it. Searches are ranked by meaning, so a query like "that 3D-printed part for the drone" can find a page with a different title. It shows a best-match score and only returns results close to the top, or says nothing was found. An Ask Unbury mode runs searches itself, rephrases weak attempts, and shows the evidence links. The library is stored locally in plain-text and binary files under Application Support.
notable: Semantic search over browser bookmarks, with a 'nothing found' result when no link is close enough
Reads Brave, Chrome, Arc, Edge and Vivaldi; Safari and Firefox not yet supported
Library stays on the Mac; only the search question is sent to a model provider for vectorising
Installable via Homebrew cask, signed and notarised
caveats: Requires an API key from OpenRouter or OpenAI; importing costs money (about $0.42 for 600 links per the page), though searches cost thousandths of a cent
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon
Safari and Firefox bookmarks are not read yet
